notes: Human (left) hand, entering from the upper left. Provenance: started from round-1 LEFT_HAND_SPEC in src/hand/skeleton.ts, re-read against aes-ref/alpha-white-geom.PNG on 4-8x zoomed crops (the step-2 start pose); calibrated in log-v2 step 2 (2026-09-21/22) and recalibrated on the step-3 builder (2026-09-23/24, D17/D18). Digit names follow user decision D2 (documentations/log/log-v2.md): THUMB = the digit with the large nail facing the viewer, coming diagonally out of the base of the palm (tip ~(562,458), D13); PINKY = the short leftmost digit curled under the palm, pointing back toward the wrist, tip ~(438,438); MIDDLE and RING = the two curled digits between, tips ~(601,523) and ~(532,505); INDEX = the extended digit reaching the contact point, tip (786,416). CALIBRATED: every joint px and r and the shape controls fitted to assets-source/reference/left-mask.png with a surrogate of build_hands.py's own SDF (minimum of the field along the camera ray through each pixel centre; Levenberg-Marquardt on the edge offset at every reference edge pixel, tighter at the fingertips, then a compass search on the count of edge px over 2 px) and checked with Blender builds, under anatomical constraints: every joint within 3x its keypoints.json uncertainty (D16); radii taper base->tip; 3D phalanx lengths near the start pose's except where D18 or the index MCP reading changes them. Step-3 controls (D17): the index knuckle (head_back 0.9, knuckle_rise 0.28, phalanx_base 0.78) with the index MCP near its reading (592,306); forearm sag on the dorsal and palmar lines; a dorsal wrist bump; a palm heel; the first dorsal interosseous; thenar 1.2; the hypothenar from 0.30 of the way to the little-finger knuckle; a thinner metacarpal base. D18: the middle and ring fingers flex toward the palm at the MCP (their PIPs 0.17 / 0.14 further from the camera than in the 2026-09-22 pose; 3D P1/P2 1.45 / 1.53). RECONSTRUCTED (not observable in one view): z depths (index and thumb toward the camera, ring and pinky away, consistent with the drawn overlaps), flat, and dorsal [0.4, 0.86, 0.32]. With the hidden middle, ring and little-finger MCPs held near their readings, the knuckle line lies about 51 deg off the hand's lateral axis toward the palm, so the metacarpal plate is a steep diagonal in cross-section; which way the back of the hand faces is an open question for the user (step-2 report). The forearm px lies outside the frame so the arm leaves the frame.
